title: Setup URI
description: Query parameters of the remote-everything://setup URI a gateway delivers an invitation in. An invitation describes one gateway and one node, and a client reads that description: there is no version, no installation id and no mode on the wire.

node.description: The node this invitation opens a door to: its globally unique node id, which every request for that node must name in the X-Remote-Everything-Node header.

node_name.description: What that node's operator calls it: 1–80 Unicode code points, no C0 or DEL control characters, not padded with whitespace. It is the node's label, not the device's — the name an invitation is issued under is the device name and travels nowhere.

origin.description: The gateway's HTTPS origin: scheme, host, optional port only; no path, query or fragment. Every request from the client goes here, and the endpoint paths below are relative to it.

invitation.description: Base64url invitation token, 43 characters. It is the secret a device redeems for a credential of its own, and the only thing that admits one: it is single-use, it is for the node above, and it expires.

fingerprint.description: SHA-256 fingerprint of the certificate the gateway serves its clients with. Present exactly when the gateway signs its own certificate (a LAN entrance): nothing else signs that gateway, so its clients have nowhere else to learn which certificate to expect.

public_key_pin.description: Base64 SHA-256 digest of that certificate's SubjectPublicKeyInfo, which survives a renewal that keeps the key. Present with fingerprint and never without it.
